findings.claim: Question 2 asks 'Name two protocols that operate at the Application layer of the TCP/IP model.' but is tariffed '1 mark - Give/Name' with the mark scheme 'One mark for any two of: HTTP, HTTPS, SMTP, IMAP. [1 mark for two correct answers]'.
findings.truth: A one-mark Give/Name item asks for one response. AQA awards a mark for each item named, so a two-item demand is a 2-mark question. Asking for two answers and paying one mark trains a wrong tariff expectation. The surgical repair keeps the 1-mark slot (the type string drives the technique-guide lookup, docs/QUESTIONS_PIPELINE.md) and asks for one protocol.
findings.evidence: spec 3.5 (protocol list: IP, TCP, HTTP, HTTPS, SMTP, IMAP) + spec 2.2 Paper 2 question types; docs/QUESTIONS_PIPELINE.md type-string table

findings.claim: Question 2 asks 'Name two types of malware that are covered in this topic.' but is tariffed '1 mark - Give/Name' with the mark scheme 'One mark for any two of: computer virus / trojan / spyware. [1 mark for two correct answers]'.
findings.truth: Same defect as F1: two required answers for a single mark. Keep the 1-mark Give/Name slot and ask for one type of malware.
findings.evidence: spec 3.6.2.2 (virus, trojan, spyware) + spec 2.2 Paper 2 question types; docs/QUESTIONS_PIPELINE.md type-string table

findings.claim: 'Worms and ransomware are not in the required list - do not bring them in.'
findings.truth: The scope statement is correct: spec 3.6.2.2 names only computer virus, trojan and spyware, and the words worm, adware and ransomware do not appear anywhere in 8525 v1.3. The instruction 'do not bring them in' is slightly stronger than the truth, because an open item such as 'name a form of malware' would still credit a worm. Not worth an edit: the three named forms always answer the question.
findings.evidence: spec 3.6.2.2; grep of the whole spec for worm / adware / ransomware returns no hits

summary: Content is aligned to 8525 v1.3 (2027 onwards): the six protocols, the four TCP/IP layers and their functions, the four network security methods, blagging/phishing/shouldering, virus/trojan/spyware, pharming, the two penetration-testing types and the five detection measures all match the spec, and the removed 2020-spec material (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, UDP, FTP, star and bus topologies) is correctly absent. All 20 knowledge-check answer keys and all 5 match-up orders recomputed and correct; no fabricated exam, paper, timing or examiner claims anywhere in the unit. The only defect is a repeated tariff error: two 'name two' items priced at one mark.
